items.topic: Source of test prompts for the 3-5 real-world decision scenarios
items.context: The deliverable requires validating gpt-image-2 on 3-5 real decision scenarios end-to-end. The prompts we pick materially affect the signal: synthetic prompts test the happy path, historical Swarm Manager decisions test real distribution, a hybrid gives both. There is no existing curated set.

options.label: Pull 3-5 UI-shaped decisions from recent Swarm Manager workshop rounds and convert each to an image-prompt
options.rationale: Highest realism — matches the actual distribution the skill will see in production. Slightly more setup (need to find decisions with image-pickable options).

options.label: Author 3-5 synthetic decision prompts spanning the expected UI dimensions (layout, palette, density, element choice)
options.rationale: Fast, covers the design space deliberately. Lower realism — may miss idiosyncrasies of how workshop agents actually phrase options.

options.label: Hybrid — 2 historical + 3 synthetic (or similar split)
options.rationale: Balances realism and design-space coverage at the cost of slightly more work.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own source or curation rule.

items.topic: Default quality tier to validate as the shipping target
items.context: gpt-image-2 exposes quality tiers with a ~4-6x cost delta (initiative doc cites ~$0.03-0.05 medium vs ~$0.13-0.20 high). 'The quality we'd ship with' is currently under-specified. Whichever tier we validate becomes the primary basis for the cost model in the conclusion.

options.label: Medium quality as default; validate high as an opt-in escape hatch
options.rationale: Cheapest per-decision cost. Aligns with 'mockup-grade' framing in the spec — decisions don't need pixel-perfect art. Risks: may look too rough to change a user's answer.

options.label: High quality as default; medium as a cost-saver setting
options.rationale: Maximizes the chance that mockups actually shift decisions (the whole point of the feature). Costs 4-6x more per decision; harder to justify at scale.

options.label: Adaptive — medium for initial option render, high for user-approved / final mockup
options.rationale: Nuanced but introduces lifecycle state we don't have yet. Probably premature for this research.

items.topic: How rigorously to compare against OpenRouter's openai/gpt-5.4-image-2 composite
items.context: The initiative doc says OpenAI-direct wins on cost because the OpenRouter composite bundles GPT-5.4 reasoning tokens — but flags that this is a working assumption the research must still verify. The spec asks us to 'justify going OpenAI-direct on cost,' which requires at least some real A/B data. Options trade rigor for research time.

options.label: Minimal spot-check — run the same 1-2 prompts through each vendor at matching quality, compare $/image and qualitative output
options.rationale: Enough to confirm/overturn the working assumption with limited time. Misses edge cases but probably sufficient for a go/no-go.

options.label: Full matrix — all 3-5 test prompts through both vendors at both quality tiers
options.rationale: Strongest basis for the cost model, but ~2x the API spend and effort for what is likely a clear-cut answer.

options.label: Skip — accept the initiative's working assumption as-is and record it in the conclusion
options.rationale: Fastest. Leaves the cost-justification claim unverified, which the spec explicitly asks us to address.

items.topic: Reference image source for the input_fidelity='high' style-consistency test
items.context: The style-consistency check requires a reference image to pass as input. Since screenshot-grounding is explicitly deferred to the downstream grounding-propagation initiative, this test is about whether reference images carry *visual style* (palette, type, density) consistently across multiple outputs — not layout faithfulness. The reference-image choice sets what 'style consistency' means here.

options.label: Use a single existing Vrooli UI screenshot as the style anchor across all test prompts
options.rationale: Closest to real production use (skill will anchor on Vrooli's own look). Requires picking a representative screenshot.

options.label: Use a generic design-system reference (e.g. a Material or shadcn example) not tied to Vrooli
options.rationale: Tests the fidelity mechanic in isolation from Vrooli specifics. Less directly applicable to the shipping use case.

options.label: Run without a reference image and rely on prompt-only style instructions
options.rationale: Tests the text-only path but doesn't exercise input_fidelity='high' at all — arguably out of scope for this decision since the research spec explicitly calls for verifying input_fidelity='high'.

items.text: Scope confirmation: this research is text-to-mockup only plus a style-consistency check of input_fidelity='high'. Screenshot/layout grounding is owned by research/bas-grounded-mockup-flow in the downstream decision-visual-grounding-propagation initiative. Keeping the boundary crisp avoids rework there.

Initiative working assumption (from ai-image-generation-foundation/orchestration-summary.md): OpenAI-direct pricing is $8 input / $30 output per 1M tokens, ~$0.03-0.05 per medium-quality image, ~$0.13-0.20 per high-quality. OpenRouter's composite bundles GPT-5.4 reasoning tokens, which is why the working assumption is it loses on cost. d3 decides how hard we verify this.

Test-harness constraint: the EnableImageGeneration toggle lives inside the planned 'swarm-manager image generate' CLI helper (execute/swarm-manager-image-cli-helper), which does not exist yet — it is a downstream execute item gated by this research. The validation harness will therefore call the OpenAI API directly (or via a throwaway wrapper) and must not assume the helper or its toggle semantics.

Sibling-item implications to watch: a no-go outcome would cascade into execute/openai-api-key-plumbing and execute/ui-mockup-generation-skill (both list this research as a dependency), and into the downstream decision-question-visuals initiative which depends on this foundation. A 'go-with-caveats' outcome (e.g. style consistency fails at medium quality) may narrow the skill's scope rather than kill the initiative.

Open gap flagged for later rounds: once d1–d4 are answered we still need to verify the exact OpenAI Images API endpoint, parameter names (quality tiers, input_fidelity), and model ID string for gpt-image-2 against current docs. The initiative doc uses the name gpt-image-2 but does not cite the endpoint schema. Later rounds will confirm this before running any real calls.
